akiec.name: Actinic Keratosis
akiec.description: Rough, scaly patch on the skin caused by years of sun exposure. Can potentially progress to squamous cell carcinoma if untreated.
akiec.recommendation: Consult a dermatologist for clinical evaluation and cryotherapy, topical treatments, or biopsy if necessary.

bcc.name: Basal Cell Carcinoma
bcc.description: The most common form of skin cancer. Usually appears as a pearly bump, flesh-colored lesion, or bleeding sore that fails to heal.
bcc.recommendation: Prompt consultation with a dermatologist or surgical oncologist for diagnostic biopsy and excision planning.

bkl.name: Benign Keratosis
bkl.description: Non-cancerous skin growth that often appears stuck-on, waxy, tan, brown, or black. Very common with age.
bkl.recommendation: Benign condition. Monitor for changes in color, size, or shape. Seek dermatologist confirmation if irritated.

df.name: Dermatofibroma
df.description: Common benign skin papule or nodule, often occurring on lower legs. May show a dimple sign when pinched.
df.recommendation: Generally harmless. No treatment required unless symptomatic or cosmetically inconvenient.

mel.name: Melanoma
mel.description: The most serious type of skin cancer. Arises in pigment-producing melanocytes. Characterized by asymmetry, irregular borders, color variation, diameter >6mm, and evolution (ABCDE rule).
mel.recommendation: URGENT dermatologist consultation required. Demands dermatoscopic exam, excisional biopsy, and staging.

nv.name: Melanocytic Nevus
nv.description: Normal, common skin mole caused by clusters of melanocytes. Typically uniform in color and shape with smooth borders.
symptoms: Even tan or dark brown color
nv.recommendation: Normal benign skin feature. Routine self-monitoring using the ABCDE criteria is advised.

vasc.name: Vascular Lesion
vasc.description: Skin growth made up of blood vessels. Ranges from small bright red cherry angiomas to elevated vascular nodules.
vasc.recommendation: Usually benign. Consult a physician if bleeding frequently or changing rapidly.

eczema.name: Eczema / Dermatitis
eczema.description: Inflammatory skin condition causing itchy, red, dry, and irritated patches. Frequently triggered by environmental factors or allergies.
eczema.recommendation: Consult a physician or dermatologist for emollients, topical corticosteroids, and allergen identification.

psoriasis.name: Psoriasis
psoriasis.description: Chronic autoimmune condition that speeds up the growth cycle of skin cells, leading to thick, silvery scales and red patches.
psoriasis.recommendation: Requires professional medical management including topical agents, phototherapy, or systemic therapy.

scc.name: Squamous cell carcinoma
scc.recommendation: Seek prompt evaluation by a dermatologist.

tinea.name: Tinea Ringworm Candidiasis
tinea.recommendation: A healthcare professional can confirm the cause and advise on treatment.
